channel.title: # 🇱🇰 This Week in Sri Lanka
channel.description: Generated by gpt-5 from 334 English News Articles published between 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-27.

item.title: Sri Lanka opened a new offshore oil and gas licensing round for four Mannar Basin blocks.
item.description: The offer covers nearly 34,000 square kilometres and targets an estimated resource potential of about 2 billion barrels of petroleum and 9 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. The Petroleum Development Authority of Sri Lanka (PDASL, the State upstream regulator) invited international exploration and production companies, citing prior gas finds drilled in 2011 and access to basin-wide geological data. The legal framework is anchored in the Petroleum Resources Act No. 21 of 2021, with earlier litigation now cleared to proceed to bidding. Authorities said successful awards could strengthen energy security and the external account, with a data room launch and bid timetable to follow Cabinet clearance.

item.title: The Bar Association asked the Supreme Court to rule that the Twenty-Second Amendment requires a referendum.
item.description: The filing by the association’s President and Secretary argued that extending the retirement ages of superior court judges to 67 and 65 could affect judicial independence and fall within Article 83, which demands people’s approval. The petition also raised whether a tenure extension and related benefits might amount to a “gratification” under the Anti‑Corruption Act No. 9 of 2023 (the national anti‑bribery law). Separate challenges and interventions were lodged by politicians across the aisle, including a bid to dismiss the case and competing requests for a popular vote. The Bill also proposes increasing the maximum number of Court of Appeal judges to 24 from 19, while introducing a special tenure cap for the Chief Justice.

item.title: Dengue cases reached 94,666 this year with 72 deaths, surveillance data showed.
item.description: The Western Province accounted for 52.92% of infections, led by Gampaha with 20,170 and Colombo with 18,775. July recorded the highest monthly total at 29,962, while 9,330 cases were logged in August up to the 26th, according to the NaDSys (National Dengue Surveillance System) platform. Authorities listed 76 high‑risk MOH areas in week 33 and urged intensified vector control. The Southern, Central and Sabaragamuwa provinces contributed a further 14.59%, 9.09% and 8.21% of cases respectively.

item.title: A chemical release forced a temporary shutdown of Ambatale and Biyagama water treatment plants.
item.description: Operations were halted as a precaution while water quality in the Kelani River was tested, and supply was gradually restored between 4:30 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. to Colombo suburbs including Kotte, Battaramulla and Wellawatta. Engineers and the National Water Supply and Drainage Board conducted on‑site checks before resuming treatment. A joint investigation with the Disaster Management Centre and security services is under way, and a police complaint has been lodged to pursue legal action against those responsible. Officials said the incident highlighted the risk from industrial activity near major intakes.

item.title: Inflation accelerated to 7.2% in July on the National Consumer Price Index.
item.description: The annual rate rose from 6.5% in June as non‑food costs stayed elevated at 9.2% year‑on‑year and food inflation climbed to 4.9%. Transport added 2.23 percentage points to the headline rate, with housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels contributing a further 1.21 points.

item.title: Cabinet approved the rollout of 300,000 smart meters with time‑of‑use tariffs.
item.description: The programme will be financed from a US$15 million Asian Development Bank concessional facility and implemented over two years by Electricity Distribution Lanka. Officials said prioritised households and businesses will receive meters capable of differential pricing by time band to improve demand management.

item.title: Tourism earnings fell 10.4% year‑on‑year in July to US$285.5 million.
item.description: Visitor arrivals slipped 1.7% to 196,845 and year‑to‑date receipts declined 11.5% to US$1.80 billion against the prior year’s US$2.03 billion. The central bank noted a revised monthly estimation method now incorporates country mix, average daily spend and length of stay.

item.title: An air‑cargo community system was set in motion to digitise airport freight flows.
item.description: The Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation convened a multi‑agency committee to design an ACCS (Air Cargo Community System) linking handlers, carriers, Customs, BOI and regulators. A feasibility study now underway will frame finance, technical architecture and process re‑engineering to cut paperwork and dwell times.

item.title: The central bank governor said the economy had recovered to almost its pre‑crisis level.
item.description: Public finances stabilised with the revenue‑to‑GDP ratio nearly doubling in three years, while disinflation and reserve rebuilding strengthened macro balance. Officials said talks with rating agencies were ongoing with a view to further upgrades following the move out of restricted default.

item.title: Tea export volumes fell 15.1% year‑on‑year in July to 20.41 million kilograms.
item.description: Packeted shipments dropped to 8.92 million kilograms and bulk consignments to 8.59 million kilograms, while instant tea rose modestly. The average FOB improved in rupees to Rs. 1,921.95 per kilogram, but slipped in dollar terms to US$5.72 compared with US$5.87 a year earlier.

item.title: El Niño‑linked forecasts pointed to above‑average rainfall in October and November.
item.description: Meteorologists said roughly 30% of the country’s annual precipitation typically falls in those two months and warned of possible reservoir surges and flood risk if totals exceed seasonal norms. The outlook indicated effects could intensify in December through February, prompting readiness planning.
